After BrockDBRequest paths

Every request takes one of a few paths. Below, each path is traced through the After BrockDB picture: who builds it, who owns it, and which principle (numbered as on the visual) does the work. Scenarios 1 and 2 are the worked examples from doc 10. The rest follow from docs 15 and 22.

The picture is built here as a pneumatic tube installation on a bench. A request is a carrier, and a carrier can only travel where a tube is laid.

    Who does what, day to day

    Platform team

    Runs the doors, sign-in, the register and the watching as products. It publishes API specs, generates connectors, keeps the golden paths current, rotates credentials and watches the run checks. The test of success is that product teams never need a ticket.

    Product teams

    Configure Banner and Workday, build on the golden paths, own their services and business rules, and run release tests.

    Business owners

    Set priorities, sign off what each BrockDB function becomes, and own the numbers.

    Ellucian

    Runs Banner and Ethos and ships releases. Brock registers and watches Ellucian's connectors.

    What's different from today

    Today

    • Power BI reads BrockDB's production tables.
    • Jobs connect straight into the database.
    • There's no gateway and no register.

    Afterwards

    • Every hop carries an identity and a request ID.
    • Every connection has an owner.
    • Banner is configured, not customised.

    About a full academic year after Banner's last go-live, the list of direct database connections reaches zero. BrockDB's history then moves to the archive, and its run costs come off the books.

    The eight principles, numbered as on the visual

    1. 1Front doors only No one reads or writes a database directly.
    2. 2Two hubs, one border Ethos joins Ellucian's products. Brock's gateway joins the campus.
    3. 3Every connection owned A published spec, an owner, a runbook and a check that it ran.
    4. 4One sign-in Brock's account for every product. Services get only what they need.
    5. 5Configure, do not customise Configure Banner. Close gaps in Ellucian's tools or on Brock's platform.
    6. 6One trusted copy Institutional reports come from Brock's data platform.
    7. 7One front per audience Students use Ellucian Experience. Staff tools start on Power Platform.
    8. 8One register Everything built has an owner, a review date and a retirement trigger.
    Fig 1 is drawn from one model of the seven paths: the hops, the tubes they use and the words under the card come from the same data.
